# multimon-ng

**Decoder for POCSAG, FLEX, AFSK, DTMF and other audio-band digital modes**

- **Version recorded:** 1.3.1
- **Categories:** `listening`, `tracking`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/EliasOenal/multimon-ng>

## What it does

Takes demodulated audio and decodes a range of classic digital modes: POCSAG and FLEX paging, AFSK at several rates, DTMF, ZVEI and others.

## Why you would want it

It is how audio from a receiver becomes text, and it is the standard back end for APRS and paging work. Piped from rtl_fm it turns a cheap dongle into a working decoder with no GUI at all.

## Before it will work

An audio source — typically piped from rtl_fm or a sound card fed by a receiver. It expects raw samples at a specific rate, which is the usual first mistake.

## How it installs

- apt: `multimon-ng`

## Known problems

It decodes whatever it is given and reports nothing when the input is wrong, so silence usually means a sample-rate or format mismatch rather than an absent signal.

## Keeping it current

- probe: apt policy
- strategy: apt_upgrade
